title: Prompt Quest: Teens & Students
description: School-life missions: plan an event with AI, catch hallucinations, protect your privacy, edit ethically, and know when not to rely on AI.
author: Prompt Quest Team

missions.title: Mission 1: Plan a School Event
missions.briefing: Your student council wants an AI-generated plan for an upcoming school event. Write a prompt that would get you a genuinely useful plan back — not generic filler.
missions.scenario: You're on the student council. The council needs a plan drafted for an event, and you've been asked to use AI to get a first draft.
missions.placeholder: Write the prompt you'd send to the AI...

requiredElements.label: A clear goal or purpose
requiredElements.hint: What is the event actually for? (e.g. "raise money for the library", "celebrate the end of the semester")

requiredElements.label: The audience
requiredElements.hint: Who is this event for? (grade level, students, parents, staff...)

requiredElements.label: A budget
requiredElements.hint: How much money is available to spend?

requiredElements.label: A date or timeframe
requiredElements.hint: When is the event, or how much time do you have to plan it?

requiredElements.label: A location
requiredElements.hint: Where will it be held? (gym, cafeteria, park, online...)

requiredElements.label: Constraints or limits
requiredElements.hint: Any rules the plan must respect? (no outside food, must end by 6pm, ADA accessible...)

requiredElements.label: A requested output format
requiredElements.hint: Ask for a specific structure — a timeline, a bulleted checklist, a table...

missions.title: Mission 2: Detect Hallucinations
missions.briefing: You asked an AI assistant for advice on running a school bake sale. Read its answer closely — one claim in here is made up. Select every claim you would want to verify before trusting it.
missions.scenario: The AI's answer sounds confident and well-organized. That doesn't mean every sentence in it is true.

claims.text: Bake sales are a classic way for school clubs to raise money for field trips and supplies.
claims.explanation: This is a well-known, general fact — no special verification needed.

claims.text: According to a 2019 National PTA study, school bake sales increase student club participation by exactly 47%.
claims.explanation: This is an oddly specific statistic attributed to a named study with no citation given. That's a classic sign of a fabricated claim — it should be verified against a real source before you repeat it.

claims.text: It's a good idea to check your school's food safety and allergy policies before selling homemade baked goods.
claims.explanation: This is standard, sensible advice and not a factual claim that needs a citation.

claims.text: Pricing items between $1 and $3 is a common approach for school bake sales.
claims.explanation: This is a reasonable, general observation, not a specific unverifiable statistic.

missions.title: Mission 3: Protect Private Information
missions.briefing: You're about to paste some background information into an AI chatbot to get help with a task. Sort each detail into the right bucket before you hit send.
missions.scenario: Not everything you know about yourself or others is safe to hand to a third-party AI tool.

items.label: Your full legal name
items.explanation: Full names aren't always sensitive, but there's rarely a reason an AI assistant needs your legal name to help with a task — leave it out by default.

items.label: An account password
items.explanation: Never share passwords or credentials with any AI tool, ever.

items.label: Details from a medical record
items.explanation: Medical information is highly sensitive. Describe symptoms or questions in general terms instead of pasting records.

items.label: A general age range (e.g. "in my 30s")
items.explanation: A general age range is usually low-risk and can help the AI tailor its answer.

items.label: A public description of your school project
items.explanation: Information that's already public or meant to be shared is generally safe to include.

missions.title: Mission 4: Improve Writing Ethically
missions.briefing: You asked an AI to polish a resume bullet point. Compare the AI's "improved" version to what you actually did, and flag anything it invented.
missions.scenario: Original bullet you wrote: "Helped organize the school food drive and made some flyers."

claims.text: Co-organized the school food drive, contributing to its overall success.
claims.explanation: This is a fair, honest rephrasing of what you actually did — fine to keep.

claims.text: Led a team of 12 volunteers to design and distribute promotional flyers.
claims.explanation: You never mentioned leading a team of 12 — the AI invented a specific, impressive-sounding detail. Accepting this would mean claiming credit for something that isn't true.

claims.text: Increased food drive donations by 30% compared to the previous year.
claims.explanation: There's no source for this statistic anywhere in your original bullet. This is a fabricated accomplishment — including it on a resume would be dishonest.

claims.text: Created flyers to promote the event.
claims.explanation: This matches what you actually said you did.

missions.title: Mission 5: Choose the Right Tool
missions.briefing: AI is a great tool for some jobs and a bad fit for others. Sort each situation into the right bucket.
missions.scenario: Good judgment means knowing when AI helps — and when it doesn't belong in the decision at all.

items.label: Brainstorming ideas for a birthday party theme
items.explanation: Low-stakes creative brainstorming is a strong use case for AI.

items.label: Summarizing a long article you don't have time to read in full
items.explanation: Summarization is a strength of AI assistants — just verify anything critical before acting on it.

items.label: Deciding what to do during a medical emergency
items.explanation: Emergencies need real emergency services, not an AI chat window. Call for help.

items.label: Getting a definitive legal answer for an active court case
items.explanation: Legal advice for a real case needs a licensed attorney who knows the specifics and jurisdiction.

items.label: Getting a first draft of a poem or short story
items.explanation: Creative first drafts are a good, low-stakes use of AI.

items.label: Checking what happened in the news in the last hour
items.explanation: AI models don't have live, up-to-the-minute information by default — use a real news source.

items.label: Sharing a friend's home address so AI can "help plan a route"
items.explanation: That's someone else's personal data — sharing it without their consent is a privacy problem, not just a judgment call about AI.
